The NICHESObject

Source: vignettes/articles/niches-object.Rmd
niches-object.Rmd

A NICHESObject is an S3 list with 15 slots, which you read with $. This guide uses NICHESv2_example, a small spatial object with 80 synthetic cells.

library(NICHESv2)
library(data.table)

data(NICHESv2_example)
obj <- NICHESv2_example
dim(obj)
#> cells genes edges  LRMs 
#>    80    50   354    15

The object is a plain list, so functions return a changed copy. Always assign the result back: obj <- add_meta_column(obj, ...).

Why long format

Most cell pairs carry no signal for most LR pairs. NICHESv2 stores only non-zero values, in keyed data.tables with one row per value. Memory use then follows how much signal exists, not how many combinations are possible.

Cell slots

Slot Contents
$cell.list Cell barcodes
$cell.data Non-zero expression, one row per (cell, gene)
$cell.meta One row per cell 
head(obj$cell.data, 3)
cell gene score score.norm
Cell_1 Gene10 7 0.106
Cell_1 Gene11 6 0.091
Cell_1 Gene12 2 0.030

In $cell.data, score is the value you supplied, and score.norm is its share of that cell’s total.

Edge slots

An edge is one directed cell pair, with an ID of the form "SendingCell|ReceivingCell".

Slot Contents
$edge.list One row per edge
$edge.data Non-zero scores, one row per (edge, LRM)
$edge.meta One row per edge, with both cells’ metadata 
head(obj$edge.data, 3)
edge LRM score score.norm
Cell_10|Cell_1 Gene9|Gene10 21 1
Cell_10|Cell_10 Gene15|Gene16 35 1
Cell_10|Cell_4 Gene9|Gene10 18 1

An LRM ID has the form "ligand|receptor". With the default normalize.method = "prop", score.norm is that LRM’s share of the edge’s total score.

$edge.meta adds Sending. and Receiving. versions of each metadata column, plus Joint. columns for text columns:

obj$edge.meta[, .(edges = .N), by = Joint.celltype][order(-edges)][1:3]
Joint.celltype edges
TypeA|TypeA 132
TypeB|TypeB 115
TypeC|TypeC 101

Neighborhood slots

These are filled in when the object is built, and all three are indexed by cell.

Slot Contents
$neighborhood.cell.list Each cell’s neighbors
$neighborhood.edge.list The edges in each cell’s neighborhood
$neighborhood.meta Neighbor and edge counts per cell 
head(obj$neighborhood.meta, 3)
cell n.neighbors n.edges
Cell_1 5 17
Cell_10 6 30
Cell_11 6 28

By default, a neighborhood holds every edge whose two cells are both in that neighborhood. add_neighborhoods(overwrite = TRUE) changes this:

edge.filter.mode Edges kept for a focal cell
"both_in_neighborhood" (default) Both cells are the focal cell or its neighbors
"any_in_neighborhood" At least one cell is the focal cell or a neighbor
"central_cell_only" One cell is the focal cell

Gene and LRM slots

Slot Contents
$gene.list, $gene.meta Genes and any annotations
$LRM.list, $LRM.meta LR pairs and their annotations 
head(obj$LRM.meta, 3)
LRM ligand receptor pathway
Gene11|Gene12 Gene11 Gene12 PathwayF
Gene13|Gene14 Gene13 Gene14 PathwayG
Gene15|Gene16 Gene15 Gene16 PathwayH

Extras

$aggregations starts empty and is filled by aggregate_NICHESObject(). $segmentation holds optional cell polygons, added with add_segmentation().

Attributes

Four attributes record how the object was built:

attr(obj, "mode")
#> [1] "spatial"
attr(obj, "sample.col")
#> NULL
attr(obj, "edge.filter.mode")
#> [1] "both_in_neighborhood"
attr(obj, "remove.autocrine")
#> [1] FALSE

Changing metadata

To add or change one column, use add_meta_column() with values named by barcode:

region <- setNames(
  ifelse(obj$cell.meta$x > 0.5, "right", "left"),
  obj$cell.meta$cell
)
obj <- add_meta_column(obj, "region", region, verbose = FALSE)
obj$edge.meta[, .(edges = .N), by = Sending.region]
Sending.region edges
left 188
right 166

add_cell_meta() replaces the whole table, so any column you leave out is lost, including coordinates. Use it only when you mean to replace everything.

Subsetting

obj[cells] takes a vector of barcodes. Each kept cell keeps its neighborhood entries and aggregation rows unchanged, while the edge slots keep only edges between kept cells.

type.a <- obj$cell.meta[celltype == "TypeA", cell]
sub <- obj[type.a]
dim(sub)
#> cells genes edges  LRMs 
#>    30    50   132    15

The aggregation guide explains how to work with subsets.

Merging

merge_NICHESObjects() combines objects from separate runs. They must share a mode and have no barcodes in common. The merged object has no neighborhoods or aggregations, so run add_neighborhoods() afterward. To process several samples in one step, use sample.col in create_NICHESObject() instead.
